counterevidence_considered.description: Falsification probe: the numerator is drawn only from retained stations, which could in principle indicate a hidden retained-subset framing; however the report explicitly assigns the 24 unobserved stations zero occurrences within the 96-station denominator and labels the result a lower bound, so the reported rate is a complete-domain rate rather than a retained-subset rate.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: numerator restricted to retained stations but denominator complete, disclosed as lower bound

source_refs.quoted_text: Occurrences observed among the retained stations: 18

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the no-issue verdict by searching for any selected or headline rate whose denominator equals the retained subset (72). I checked the selected-result line, the exposure-denominator line, the workflow string that builds the selected result, and the limitations section: the denominator constant used is SCHEDULED_STATIONS = 96, the arithmetic 18/96 = 0.1875 is consistent with the complete-domain denominator, and results/report.md L0019 explicitly states no screened-subset rate is reported. I also checked whether the 72-station count appears anywhere as an exposure base and found it only as a descriptive count on results/report.md L0009. No retained-subset denominator underlies the reported claim, so the in-scope mismatch could not be demonstrated.
